title: Writing a CSV file
label: CSV writing
description: Write the events table to a CSV file with writeCsv(). The table is read before the clock starts. Writing is plain PHP.
workload: 1,000,000 rows, 5 columns: id int, key int, g string, x double with about 2% NA, t datetime

check.note: Every implementation returned the same number of result rows in every run.

method: Each run is a fresh PHP process. The clock runs from the writeCsv() call until the file is written. Process startup and reading the input are excluded. Each implementation runs one warm-up, then the implementations alternate for 7 rounds in a rotated order.
time_spent_in: the PHP process, with SQLite and Polars running in it as linked libraries
memory_method: Peak anonymous memory is RssAnon from /proc/PID/status, sampled every millisecond by peakmem (phit's bench/peakmem.c), for the whole process, with the input tables loaded. peak_rss_mib is the kernel's peak resident set size from getrusage(), which also counts mapped file pages. php_peak_mib is memory_get_peak_usage(true) at the end of the run; it does not count memory that SQLite or Polars allocate outside PHP's allocator.
reproduce: cc -O2 -o ~/.local/bin/peakmem bench/peakmem.c  # in a phit checkout
